pr.title: MIR inliner maintains unused var_debug_info
pr.description: Only `full` debuginfo level promises variable-level debug information, but the MIR inline pass needlessly preserved the local variable debug info for the `limited` level too.
pr.author: kornelski

analysis.originalLogic: In `inline_call` in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/inline.rs`, after inserting the callee's local declarations and source scopes into the caller, the pass decided whether to append the callee's `var_debug_info` using `unwrap_or(tcx.sess.opts.debuginfo != DebugInfo::None)`. Thus, when no explicit `inline_mir_preserve_debug` override was set, variable debug info was retained for every debuginfo level other than `None`, including `Limited`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation preserved the inlined callee's `var_debug_info` when compiling with `-C debuginfo=1` (`DebugInfo::Limited`) and no `-Zinline-mir-preserve-debug`, even though limited debuginfo does not promise variable-level information. The fix changes the fallback condition to `unwrap_or(tcx.sess.opts.debuginfo == DebugInfo::Full)`, so default preservation happens only for full debuginfo; the explicit override still forces preservation independently of the debuginfo level.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR inlining of a callee that carries `var_debug_info` entries (parameters or locals) into a caller, with `-C debuginfo` set to none, limited, or full, and optionally `-Zinline-mir-preserve-debug` enabled. The test domain uses `#[inline(always)]` callees and an `#[inline(never)]` caller so the Inline MIR pass output can be checked for `debug binding =>`, `debug arg1 =>`, `debug local1 =>`, and `debug _local2 =>`.
analysis.summary: A bug fix in the MIR Inline pass: default preservation of callee `var_debug_info` during inlining was too broad because it treated any non-`None` debuginfo as requiring variable-level debug info. Preservation must occur by default only for `DebugInfo::Full`; explicit `-Zinline-mir-preserve-debug` remains an independent override. The regression test distinguishes PRESERVE, FULL, NONE, and LIMITED revisions.
analysis.trigger: Compile with MIR inlining enabled and `-C debuginfo=1` (`DebugInfo::Limited`) without `-Zinline-mir-preserve-debug`, while the inlined callee has variable debug info. The old fallback condition `debuginfo != DebugInfo::None` evaluated true and appended the callee's `var_debug_info` to the caller.
preconditions: The Inline MIR pass successfully inlines a call whose callee body has non-empty `var_debug_info`.
No explicit `-Zinline-mir-preserve-debug` override is supplied, so the fallback debuginfo-level check is used.
Debuginfo is `Limited` (`-C debuginfo=1`), not `None` and not `Full`.
The caller body has already received the callee's local declarations and source scopes before the `var_debug_info` append decision.
pitfalls: Do not use `debuginfo != DebugInfo::None` as the default preservation condition; `Limited` is intentionally excluded because only `full` promises variable-level debug information.
Do not remove the explicit `-Zinline-mir-preserve-debug` override: the patch states it is enabled when building the standard library so MIR-opt results stay consistent with or without debuginfo.

The PRESERVE revision uses `-C debuginfo=0 -Zinline-mir-preserve-debug` and must still show debug entries, while NONE and LIMITED must not; treating the override as equivalent to debuginfo level would miss the intended behavior.
This is a debug-info retention bug, not a claim that inlining itself failed or that generated code semantics changed.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a `//@ test-mir-pass: Inline` regression test with four revisions: PRESERVE `-O -C debuginfo=0 -Zinline-mir-preserve-debug`, FULL `-O -C debuginfo=2`, NONE `-O -C debuginfo=0`, and LIMITED `-O -C debuginfo=1`. Force inlining through `#[inline(always)]` functions and inspect the `(inlined ...)` MIR. Assert `debug binding =>`, `debug arg1 =>`, `debug local1 =>`, and `debug _local2 =>` are present for PRESERVE and FULL, and use `NONE-NOT` and `LIMITED-NOT` to assert they are absent for NONE and LIMITED. The new test file is `tests/mir-opt/inline_var_debug_info_kept.rs`.
evidence: Only `full` debuginfo level promises variable-level debug information, but the MIR inline pass needlessly preserved the local variable debug info for the `limited` level too.
